subject: Re: FinTrust - follow-up on access controls & support access
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Kessler <aisha.kessler@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinTrust - follow-up on access controls & support access

Hi Aisha — great to meet today, and thanks for walking us through your ingestion and retention workflow. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we’re aligned:

- Summary of ask: FinTrust needs documentation and confirmation around role-based access (RBAC), least-privilege enforcement, break-glass procedures for emergency support access, and retention/logging controls for PII-derived data.
- What we covered: Redwood’s RBAC model (org/team/role hierarchy), support access workflow (time-limited break-glass with approvals + audit log), data retention tooling (configurable per-route retention TTLs), and logging controls (token-level, request/response redaction options).

Action items: 
1) I’ll attach our SOC 2 report and a support-access matrix that shows roles and required approvals (attached).
2) Dylan will provide a short bulleted doc on how we implement break-glass (who approves, how long access lasts, and audit trail).
3) Can you confirm which FinTrust roles need break-glass ability vs. read-only support access? That will help us scope the canary policy for Dedicated capacity.

Proposed next call: Thu 22 Jul, 10:00 AM PT — 20 min to walk the support access flow and alignment on retention windows.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments:
- SOC2-report-2027.pdf (pdf, redacted sections)
- support-access-matrix.pdf (xls-style matrix)
From: Aisha Kessler <aisha.kessler@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTrust - follow-up on access controls & support access

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap and appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifying questions from our security team after reviewing the SOC2 doc: 

1) Break-glass approval: in a production emergency, who in Redwood can approve a temporary elevation? We need a primary and backup approver listed for audit.
2) Least privilege enforcement: do roles have immutable permissions or can permissions be scoped dynamically per-customer (for example, FinTrust needs to ensure support agents never see raw PII unless explicitly approved)?
3) Audit logs: is the full request/response body persisted in logs by default? If so, can that be redacted at route or tenant level prior to storage?

We’ll pull together the internal roles that may require break-glass (most likely SRE lead and on-call security), and will confirm before the call.

Also — if you can send the short break-glass write-up Dylan mentioned, that would be great to have ahead of Thu’s call.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Security Operations, FinTrust
aisha.kessler@fintrust.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Kessler <aisha.kessler@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTrust - follow-up on access controls & support access

Hi Aisha — quick answers inline below and a short breakdown attached. See attached: support-access-matrix.pdf (matrix) and break-glass-process.txt (plain text summary).

1) Break-glass approval
- Primary approver: Security Lead (Redwood) — name/role recorded in audit.
- Backup approver: Head of SRE (Redwood).
- In emergencies, our on-call SRE can grant temporary access but the grant is logged and retroactively requires a secondary approval within 24 hours.

2) Least privilege enforcement
- Roles are configurable per-customer. We support tenant-scoped role mappings so support agents are not granted access to raw PII by default. Any elevation is explicit and time-limited.

3) Audit logs and redaction
- By default request metadata and headers are logged. Full request/response bodies are not persisted by default for routes flagged as PII-sensitive. We provide route-level redaction rules and tenant-level policies to prevent storage of raw PII.

Next steps:
- Marissa and I will join Thu’s call to walk the break-glass flow and show the admin UI for time-limited grants.
- Aisha, please send the list of FinTrust roles to map to Redwood roles prior to the call.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com
From: Aisha Kessler <aisha.kessler@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700

Thanks — that all sounds good. Confirmed for Thu 22 Jul at 10:00 AM PT. I’m attaching the FinTrust role list (internal) to prepare mapping:

- SRE Lead (on-call)
- SecOps Manager
- Platform Support (tier 2)

We’ll aim to restrict break-glass to SRE Lead + SecOps Manager; Platform Support should be read-only unless elevated.

See you on Thursday.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Security Operations, FinTrust
